# AI Spend Guard

> Universal financial firewall and budget-as-code toolkit for AI apps, agents, media generation, tools, and paid APIs.

Repository: https://github.com/0xatlas96/ai-spend-guard
License: MIT
Runtime: Node.js 20+; NodeSqliteStore requires Node.js 22.5+

## Start here

- README.md — product overview, installation, examples, guarantees
- AGENTS.md — instructions for coding agents contributing to this repository
- docs/architecture.md — design and transaction invariant
- docs/threat-model.md — trust boundary and failure semantics
- docs/cookbook.md — common deployment policies
- SECURITY.md — vulnerability reporting and security model
- CONTRIBUTING.md — contribution workflow
- ROADMAP.md — planned work

## Core API

- SpendFirewall — main policy-based financial firewall
- FirewallReservation — reserve, resize/topUp, settle, release
- MemoryStore — in-process transactional ledger
- JsonFileStore — local/single-host persistent ledger
- NodeSqliteStore — zero-third-party-dependency SQLite ledger on Node 22.5+
- PostgresStore (subpath `ai-spend-guard/postgres`) — multi-host transactional ledger
- createVercelAiSpendMiddleware (subpath `ai-spend-guard/vercel-ai`) — AI SDK 7 generate/stream guard
- startSpendGuardServer — authenticated HTTP sidecar + local dashboard
- verifyBudgetContract — versioned config + policy tests + spend plan verification
- runPolicyTests — deterministic policy contract tests
- simulateSpendPlan — budget-as-code pre-deployment cost simulation
- inspectFirewallConfig — configuration safety doctor

## Core safety invariant

For every protected paid operation:

1. calculate a conservative upper-bound estimate
2. atomically check all matching enforced policies
3. reserve that estimate before provider dispatch
4. execute the paid operation
5. settle actual cost
6. never silently discard an ambiguous potentially billed operation

Outstanding reservations count against budget so concurrent requests cannot all consume the same remaining headroom.

## Important constraints

- Unknown estimates fail closed by default.
- Provider pricing is caller-owned because commercial prices change.
- Calls that bypass the firewall are invisible to it.
- Multi-host deployments should use the transactional PostgresStore or another correct shared LedgerStore.
- The HTTP sidecar requires bearer authentication on non-loopback binds.
- Vercel streaming calls settle on the final finish/usage event; ambiguous endings remain reserved.
- Ambiguous provider failures keep the reservation open for reconciliation.
- Do not introduce telemetry or network calls into the core.
- Do not weaken requiredContext, grouped-budget isolation, transaction semantics, or fail-closed behavior without tests and documentation.

## Quick verification

```bash
npm install
npm run ci
```

Starter workflow:

```bash
node dist/cli.js init
node dist/cli.js doctor
node dist/cli.js test-policies --file policy-tests.json
node dist/cli.js plan --file spend-plan.json
```
